title: Boolean Search for Social Listening: Operators by Tool (2026)
summary: Social listening Boolean search differs by tool. See how 8 vendors' docs write AND, OR, NOT, proximity and wildcards, plus a portable core and a test list.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** In the social listening Boolean search documentation of eight tools we opened, AND, OR and a way to exclude terms appear in all eight, but exclusion is written four ways, seven tools document proximity in seven written forms, and wildcards are documented by only four. The portable core of a query is AND, OR, exclusion and quoted phrases; everything else should be rewritten and tested per tool.


A query that works in one tool can return something different in another, and one operator can be the cause.


Social listening Boolean search looks standard, yet the pages we opened spell exclusion four ways and proximity seven ways. Copy a query between tools without translating it and you change what you count.


This post sets out what eight vendors' pages and one X developer page show, as read in November 2026. We ran no query in any product, so every example is untested; the patterns, examples and checklist are our suggested approach.


## How do AND, OR, NOT, quotes and parentheses work in social listening Boolean search?


AND and OR are documented in all eight tools, though Emplifi and Sprout set them in a builder. Exclusion is written` AND NOT` ,` NOT` ,` {NOT}` or` -term` , or entered in a separate field.


**Boolean search** : a way to combine keywords with operators such as AND, OR and NOT so that a listening tool collects only mentions that match your logic.


Strings are copied from each page with placeholder terms. "Not published" means not published on the pages we opened; "builder" means set in the interface with no typed string shown; "undated" means no calendar date on the page. Talkwalker is per Talkwalker's developer documentation, whose pages refer to a query editor, so we do not claim its product behaves the same. Emplifi is per Emplifi's Listening General Guide; the docs also list a newer Listening Hub guide we did not open.

No vendor page in the matrix states a precedence rule. X's developer page does: operators joined by AND are combined first, then OR, and operators are case-insensitive. (Source:[X developer docs, undated, checked Nov 2026](https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/search/integrate/build-a-query) ) Pulsar's page says AND, OR, NOT and its target operators must be capitalized; the Talkwalker, Awario and Brand24 pages do not say, and Brand24's examples show both` {AND}` and` {and}` . Because precedence is unpublished, "always use parentheses" is our suggested approach.


Awario's page warns that a plain` AND NOT` removes a term anywhere in a document and suggests pairing it with` near/n` . (Source:[Awario, undated, checked Nov 2026](https://awario.com/help/boolean-search/boolean-syntax-and-operators/) ) Pulsar's page says NOT cannot be used alone, Emplifi's page requires at least one include condition per query, and Brand24's page says to leave no space between an operator and its term.


## How do proximity, wildcards and case sensitivity differ?


Seven tools document proximity in seven written forms, and the number counts differently on different pages. Four tools document wildcards.


**Proximity operator** : an operator that requires two terms to appear within a set number of words of each other.


**Wildcard** : a character such as` *` that stands in for part of a word.

The same number is not the same distance. Awario's` near/4` allows up to 4 words in between, YouScan's` /2` allows 1 word between, Emplifi's` NEAR(3)` means up to three words apart, Talkwalker's` ~5` counts "jumps", SentiOne's` ~n` counts actions including swaps, and Pulsar caps` ~n` at 6.` NEAR/5` ,` ~5` and` /5` are not equivalent, so re-set the number in each tool. The seven forms leave out the order-fixing variants (` ONEAR/x` ,` onear/n:` ,` NEAR/n` ); SentiOne's page says its pipe form runs in both orders and` NEAR/n` fixes the order.


Default matching differs too. Talkwalker's page says no stemming is done, YouScan's page says it finds different word forms automatically, and Sprout's page describes fuzzy matching or word conjugation unless Exact Match is selected.


Wildcards are the least portable common operator. SentiOne's page says not to combine quotes and an asterisk, and per Emplifi's documentation, wildcards are not supported in keywords. Awario's page shows` *` only inside` link:` , and Brand24 and Sprout do not publish a wildcard operator on the pages we opened.


## Which field, source, language, hashtag and handle operators do the docs show?


These operators diverge most, and several are tied to X data, an add-on, real-time only access or a "premium" label.


**Field operator** : an operator that limits a term to part of a post or to a property of it, such as the title, author, hashtag, language, country or source.

Check which sources your[social listening platform](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) collects first. Sprout's page says from-user, mention and to-user terms work for all sources but best with X, and its location filter drops every message without a location tied to it on X. Pulsar's page lists` BY_TWITTER` and` IN_URL` under X-only operators. Talkwalker, Awario, Brand24 and SentiOne do not publish which operators apply to which sources.


Pulsar's page also publishes placement rules: its language, location and media lists use OR only, sit in AND with the rest of the expression and cannot be negated.

Modes change what a string means. Emplifi and Sprout are builder-first, with keyword boxes and groups rather than a typed Boolean string, though Sprout also takes typed shorthands. Emplifi's page says filters and hidden operators count toward length.


## Which query patterns carry across tools, and where do they break?


The patterns documented by at least six of eight tools are AND, OR, exclusion and quoted phrases. The list below is our suggested approach; counts come from the pages we opened.


1.


**Synonyms in one OR group** , a context term in an AND group. Documented by 8 of 8.


2.


**Exclusions** as separate, narrow terms. Documented by 8 of 8; X's page advises against negating grouped operators.


3.


**Phrases in quotes** , with no wildcard inside. Documented by 6 of 8.


4.


**Parentheses** around every mixed AND and OR group. Typed grouping in 5 of 8; no precedence rule in the matrix.


5.


**Proximity** instead of bare AND, with the number re-set per tool. Documented by 7 of 8.


6.


**Tool-specific operators** , written per tool. Documented by 4 (wildcards), 3 (case), 5 (hashtag or handle), 4 typed or 6 with builder filters (language) and 4 typed or 6 with builder choices (source) of 8.


7.


**Builder-first tools:** the same logic as groups and fields. Check the preview.

## How do you test a social listening Boolean search query before you trust it?


Our suggested approach: test precision, recall, exclusions, operator behavior and length, in that order.


1.


**Precision sample.** Read a fixed sample of matches from the first day and count the irrelevant ones. Repeat after every edit.


2.


**Recall check.** Assemble a small set of relevant posts found by hand and confirm the query returns them. Include a few where the brand appears only in speech or visuals, which text matching can miss (see[mentions text search misses](https://syncly.app/blog/short-form-video-mentions-social-listening-misses) ).


3.


**Exclusion test.** Add one exclusion, re-read the sample, keep or drop it.


4.


**Operator behavior test.** Run one AND, one OR, one exclusion and one proximity on posts you can see, because default matching and the meaning of n differ.


5.


**Length check.** Compare the query's character count with the limit the page states for that tool and source.


6.


**Port test.** Before copying a query between tools, translate each operator from the matrices and mark every "not published" cell as a question for the vendor.


Recall depends on how far back a tool collects. Emplifi's page says edits apply only to future mentions unless you duplicate the query with a past date range, and Pulsar's page says some operators on X may stop historic data being retrieved. Our[historical data explained](https://syncly.app/blog/social-listening-historical-data-what-12-tools-mean-(2026)) post covers how tools define that window.


## Key Takeaways


-


AND, OR and an exclusion method are documented by all eight tools, but exclusion is written four ways and two tools use a separate field.


-


The proximity number is not equivalent across tools: seven written forms, with distance counted differently on different pages.


-


Wildcards (4 of 8), case matching (3), hashtag or handle terms (5) and typed language and source operators (4 each) are tool-specific; several depend on X data, an add-on or a premium label.


-


No vendor page in the matrix states a precedence rule, so parenthesize mixed AND and OR groups and test the result in each tool.


The portable core of a query is AND, OR, exclusion and quoted phrases, and everything else should be rewritten and tested per tool. Treat a Boolean string as a hypothesis about your brand's conversation, because each tool reads it differently.
